title: Florida AI Laws

reading.body:
Florida's only AI-related law is a resolution recognizing the Tampa Bay area as a cybersecurity and AI innovation region, not a rule that governs anyone.

The law, S1816, passed on 2026-03-12. It does three things: it names CyberBay as a cybersecurity and AI innovation region, it acknowledges the state's standing in cybersecurity preparedness and digital defense, and it affirms public-private collaboration on cyber readiness. None of that imposes an obligation, a disclosure duty, or a compliance deadline on any company.

That distinction matters for anyone reading state AI law as a map of where builders face real constraints. A recognition measure and a binding statute both count as AI-related here, so a count of one does not mean Florida regulates AI. It means Florida has said something about it.

What this does not cover is the rest of Florida's legislative output. The data holds one law and no failed bills, no pending bills, and no effective dates beyond the passage date. It also says nothing about data centers, power, or compute in the state, so no conclusion about Florida's role in AI infrastructure can be drawn from it.

Enacted AI laws in Florida

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • S1816: CyberBay passed 2026-03-12

    The Florida Senate recognizes CyberBay as a cybersecurity and artificial intelligence innovation region within the Tampa Bay area, acknowledges Florida's national leadership in cybersecurity preparedness and digital defense, and affirms the importance of continued public-private collaboration to strengthen cyber readiness and economic resilience.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Florida. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
